name: Cambridge CIL draft charging schedule consultation issue
fact: Cambridge Cabinet considered the draft CIL charging schedule on 10 February 2026 with supporting infrastructure, viability, instalment and consultation documents.
gate: Draft schedule evidence is plan-making/process context and is not an operative site charge until adopted and effective.

name: Leeds CIL spending and status check
fact: Leeds publishes how CIL is split between neighbourhood and strategic funds, links the 2024/25 IFS and provides an application-level CIL status check for compliance, amount due/paid and discharge.
gate: Authority fund percentages are not site liability; exact application CIL status must be checked separately.

name: Leeds Infrastructure Funding Statement 2024/25
fact: Leeds' 2024/25 IFS reports CIL and S106 receipts, expenditure, retained balances and future infrastructure priorities and notes developer-contribution data is a point-in-time estimate subject to change.
gate: IFS finance is a snapshot and not a parcel-specific commitment or final contribution calculation.

name: Oxford Infrastructure Funding Statement 2024/25
fact: Oxford's 2024/25 IFS reports CIL/S106 receipts, allocations and spend, identifies S106 trigger information for listed agreements and states future CIL programme allocations may change during budget setting.
gate: Listed project allocation or agreement trigger is not proof the target parcel has paid, discharged or delivered the obligation.

name: Oxford CIL Charging Schedule August 2025
fact: Oxford publishes its August 2025 CIL Charging Schedule and explains annual IFS reporting of CIL and S106 collection, spend and retained balances.
gate: Charging schedule rates require exact permission date, chargeable floorspace, indexation and relief/exemption checks before liability can be calculated.

name: Oxford what CIL will be spent on
fact: Oxford explains the IFS summarises prior-year developer contributions and identifies infrastructure items CIL is intended to support over future years.
gate: A future spending list is an authority intention and not a binding delivery promise to a particular development.

name: Bristol Infrastructure Funding Statement
fact: Bristol's IFS page publishes the 2024/25 CIL report and infrastructure list and currently marks the 2024/25 Section 106 report as coming soon.
gate: A missing current S106 report must not be interpreted as zero S106 obligations or spend.

name: Bristol Section 106 money allocation
fact: Bristol publishes quarterly Section 106 money information, including a January-March 2026 summary and balances held for infrastructure allocation.
gate: Money held or allocated at area/city level does not establish a target site's obligation status or mitigation delivery.

name: Merton Section 106 agreements and planning obligations
fact: Merton explains that individual S106 agreements can be viewed through the linked planning application record and publishes annual infrastructure funding statements for CIL/S106 activity.
gate: Planning-register visibility is necessary evidence, but agreement presence alone does not show obligations are triggered, discharged or outstanding.

name: Milton Keynes planning obligations
fact: Milton Keynes publishes planning-obligation process, monitoring/accountability, tariff/CIL, infrastructure funding statement, 2026/27 fees and public-facing S106 information.
gate: Process/fees and public modules do not replace exact legal agreement and compliance evidence for a site.

name: Reading planning policy and IFS index
fact: Reading's planning-policy page links the 2024/25 Infrastructure Funding Statement and explains it reports collection, allocation and spend of developer contributions plus future spend.
gate: Annual contribution reporting is authority-level evidence and not an exact parcel liability or funding guarantee.

name: Reading Local Plan examination evidence index
fact: Reading's examination page lists the adopted CIL Charging Schedule, Infrastructure Funding Statement, affordable housing SPD and S106 Planning Obligations SPD among relevant policy documents.
gate: Document listing identifies applicable evidence sources but does not establish which contribution applies to a target proposal.

name: Brighton and Hove Infrastructure Funding Statement 2024/25
fact: Brighton & Hove's 2024/25 IFS reports CIL and S106 developer contributions, including amounts received/spent and infrastructure types the council plans or may fund.
gate: IFS planned funding categories are not site-specific infrastructure commitments or proof of mitigation delivery.

name: Brent Infrastructure Funding Statement 2024-25 decision record
fact: As of 24 July 2026 Brent's issue page records the 2024-25 IFS as a key decision for determination, with a decision due 27 July 2026.
gate: A scheduled/future decision must not be treated as approved before the recorded decision is made and published.

name: Brent Infrastructure Funding Statement 2023/24 approved
fact: Brent Cabinet approved publication of the 2023/24 IFS in December 2024.
gate: An older approved IFS is historical reporting and must not override a newer 2024/25 statement or current site agreement.

name: Dover IFS 2024/25 S106 receipts
fact: Dover's 2024/25 IFS reports S106 opening balances and contributions received by infrastructure type during the financial year.
gate: Receipt totals are authority finance; they do not identify whether a target site's obligation is outstanding, discharged or available for a particular project.

name: Dover IFS 2024/25 S106 expenditure
fact: Dover reports S106 expenditure/transfers during 2024/25 and distinguishes transfers to external bodies and internal project use.
gate: Transfer/spend reporting does not prove infrastructure is physically complete or that a target development's mitigation has been satisfied.

name: Dover IFS future spending priorities
fact: Dover's 2024/25 IFS sets future infrastructure and affordable-housing spending priorities in the context of the adopted October 2024 Local Plan and its infrastructure/developer-contribution policy.
gate: Future priorities are planning/funding intentions, not guaranteed project delivery or parcel-specific mitigation.

name: Arun Infrastructure Funding Statement and developer contributions
fact: Arun publishes the 2024/25 IFS and explicitly warns developer-contribution data is a point-in-time estimate that may be updated; pre-April-2019 S106 transaction coverage can be limited.
gate: Snapshot and incomplete historic transaction coverage require exact agreement/register evidence before parcel conclusions.

name: Southampton spending the Community Infrastructure Levy
fact: Southampton publishes its 2024/25 IFS and annual CIL receipt breakdown, distinguishing local, strategic and administration portions.
gate: City-wide receipts and fund splits are not a target development's CIL liability or a promise of infrastructure at its location.

name: MCIL2 adoption decision MD2413
fact: The Mayoral decision approved MCIL2 to supersede MCIL1 for relevant permissions from 1 April 2019 and ended the older Crossrail S106 funding SPG for permissions from that date.
gate: Permission date determines which regime applies; do not mix superseded MCIL1/Crossrail S106 rules with later permissions.

name: Arun Local Development Scheme infrastructure funding context
fact: Arun's current Local Development Scheme explains the Local Plan/Infrastructure Delivery Plan identifies infrastructure needs and that delivery can use S106 contributions and CIL receipts.
gate: Plan-level infrastructure mechanisms do not establish a site's exact contribution, trigger or delivery outcome.
